Title: A production bastion host accepts SSH from the entire internet
Detail: sg-bastion allows TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 on cgi-prod-bastion-01, a public host whose instance role can read customer exports. The rule was added by ext-ops-contractor on 14 Mar 2025 during a database incident, with no change ticket, and never removed. The default network ACL allows the same traffic, the host accepts IMDSv1 and its volume is unencrypted.
Root cause: Temporary incident access never reverted; no configuration baseline (CG-03); no change record for cloud changes; no alert on security group changes (4.10).
Remediation: Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 rule today. Replace the bastion with Session Manager, which needs no inbound port. Require IMDSv2. Add a Config rule for unrestricted SSH with an alert.

Title: A contractor login from the March 2025 incident is still live, with no MFA
Detail: ext-ops-contractor has a console password with no MFA, full administrator rights through a directly attached policy, and an access key created on day one and never used. Last sign-in 02 Apr 2025 (562 days). The engagement ended in April 2025. No leaver ticket exists.
Root cause: Contractors sit outside the HR-driven leaver process (the OFI-06 population gap); CloudCo users are not federated with OfficeCo (1.20), so nothing cascades; the monthly orphaned-account reconciliation (CGI-POL-003 s4.7.3) has never run for CloudCo.
Remediation: Disable the console password and delete the key today. Review CloudTrail for any activity since 02 Apr 2025 (eu-central-1 only - see limitation L-02). Root cause is fixed by CF-09.

Title: A former consultant's cloud account can still read a 2024 customer database export
Detail: cgi-data-migration-2024 holds a full customer database export from the June 2024 migration (3 objects, Restricted under CGI-POL-004 s4.1.3). Bucket-level Block Public Access was switched off on 11 Jun 2024 and the bucket policy grants read and list to the migration consultant's CloudCo account. No data processing agreement is on file and the consultant is not in the CGI-TPR-001 inventory, because the engagement falls outside its 12-month finance lookback. S3 read events are not logged, so nobody can tell whether the export was read after the engagement ended.
Root cause: One-off project data never disposed of (CGI-POL-004 s4.2 retention never executed - OFI-05); no external-access analyzer; no data discovery; vendor discovery did not include access-based sources.
Remediation: Remove the cross-account statement today. The CTO records a breach-assessment decision under CGI-POL-005 s5.6.3, counting from awareness on 15 Oct 2026. Preserve the evidence, then delete the export under the CGI-POL-004 disposal rule with a deletion record. Obtain written confirmation that the consultant holds no copies. Enable IAM Access Analyzer everywhere. Record the consultant in CGI-TPR-001 as a terminated relationship.

Title: Account-wide S3 Block Public Access is switched off
Detail: All four account-level settings have been false since 22 Feb 2024, when they were switched off to publish website assets from cgi-www-assets. Bucket-level settings protect 3 of 5 buckets, but nothing stops a new bucket or an edited policy from going public, and no SCP protects the setting. No customer data is public today: manual inspection of the one public bucket found 1,412 web assets only.
Root cause: The account-wide guardrail was removed to serve one public use case instead of putting the public assets behind a content delivery network.
Remediation: Serve cgi-www-assets through CloudFront with Origin Access Control. Turn on all four account-level settings. Add an SCP denying changes to Block Public Access except through a break-glass role. Add Config rules for account-level and bucket-level public access.

Title: Customer data is encrypted, but with keys Cypher does not manage
Detail: cgi-prod-exports and cgi-prod-app-attachments use SSE-S3, the default. No customer-managed KMS key exists. The trail logs are SSE-S3 and EBS encryption by default is off. SSE-S3 is real encryption, but S3 decrypts an object for anyone the bucket policy allows, including everyone if the bucket goes public. It gives no protection against R-005's threat. SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key adds a second permission (kms:Decrypt) that an anonymous or foreign account does not hold.
Root cause: No cryptography standard (A.8.24 Not started; ISO-11); CloudCo CUEC 4 never accepted.
Remediation: Create customer-managed keys for exports, attachments and logs, with key policies limited to the application roles. Enable rotation. Switch default bucket encryption to SSE-KMS with bucket keys and re-encrypt existing objects. Turn on EBS encryption by default.

Title: The cloud's diary covers one region of one account, and it is not sealed
Detail: One single-region trail (eu-central-1, production, since May 2023). Nothing is recorded in the management or staging accounts, in us-east-1 where the backups are copied, or in any other region. Log file validation is off, the trail bucket has no access logging, and no S3 data events are captured.
Root cause: Trail created at account setup and never revisited; REC-07 not started.
Remediation: One organisation trail from the management account covering all regions: management events plus S3 data events for Restricted buckets, validation on, SSE-KMS, delivered to a dedicated log-archive account with access logging and Object Lock.

Title: Nobody is told when something bad happens in the cloud
Detail: All 15 monitoring recommendations fail. Zero metric filters, rules, alarms or subscribers exist, because CloudTrail is not delivered to any log platform. AWS Config and Security Hub run only in production eu-central-1 and us-east-1, switched on 05 Oct 2026 for this review, and their findings go to nobody. GuardDuty is off.
Root cause: No monitoring owner and no alert-handling procedure (A.8.16 Not started; OFI-03).
Remediation: Enable Config, Security Hub and GuardDuty in every account and region with a delegated administrator. Create EventBridge rules for the 4.1-4.15 events, routed through SNS to the ChatCo security channel and email. Write an alert runbook that maps alerts to the CGI-POL-005 severity levels. Keep 90 days of handled-alert records.

Title: The root user is used for billing and protected by a phone app, not a hardware key
Detail: All three root users have authenticator-app MFA and no access keys. CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3 requires a hardware device; none is registered. The management-account root user signed in 4 times in 90 days for invoices and a card change, with no alert and no record, and its credentials are not sealed.
Root cause: Billing was never delegated to IAM; there is no root runbook.
Remediation: Register two FIDO hardware keys per root user. Turn on IAM access to Billing and give Finance a billing role. Alert the CTO and CEO on any root sign-in (4.3). Seal the credentials and document each use. Consider centralised root access management to remove root credentials from production and staging. Until the keys are installed, operate proposed exception EXC-004.

Title: Engineers hold full administrator rights, with phishable MFA, on accounts nobody manages centrally
Detail: cgi-ops-fullaccess (Action '*', Resource '*') is attached to Engineering-Admins (4 users) and to the contractor. No separate administrative accounts exist (CGI-POL-002 s4.4.1). Users are created per account, not federated with OfficeCo. All 7 MFA devices are authenticator apps, contrary to s4.3.3. No access analyzer runs and no quarterly privileged access review has ever been performed (OFI-15).
Root cause: The start-up permission model was never revisited; CloudCo CUEC 3 was never accepted.
Remediation: IAM Identity Center federated with OfficeCo. Permission sets: read-only by default, time-bound elevation to admin. FIDO2 keys for administrators. Delete IAM users. Access analyzers for external and unused access. First quarterly review under REC-02.

Title: Deployments use a 412-day-old access key
Detail: codeco-deploy uses a long-lived access key, never rotated, stored as a CodeCo repository secret. It can update ECS services and write to cgi-www-assets.
Root cause: The deployment pipeline was set up before OpenID Connect federation was considered; no rule covers machine credentials.
Remediation: Federate CodeCo's CI service to an IAM role with OpenID Connect and short-lived credentials, scoped to the deploy actions. Delete the key.

Title: The cloud password rule is weaker than Cypher's own policy
Detail: Minimum length 8 and no reuse prevention in all three accounts. CGI-POL-002 requires 14, or 16 for privileged accounts, and every CloudCo console user is privileged.
Root cause: The CloudCo default was never changed after the policy pack was approved.
Remediation: Set minimum length to 16 and reuse prevention to 24 today. The rule falls away once access is federated (CF-09).

Title: Network traffic goes unrecorded and default network rules are untouched
Detail: No VPC flow logs. Default security groups in the production VPC and every default VPC still allow internal and outbound traffic.
Root cause: Defaults accepted at account creation; no network baseline (A.8.20 Not started).
Remediation: Flow logs (rejected traffic at minimum) to the log archive. Strip the default security group rules and delete unused default VPCs.

Title: S3 accepts plain-HTTP requests and has no delete protection
Detail: No bucket denies non-TLS requests. MFA Delete is off. Only the root user can switch it on, which conflicts with eliminating root use (RC-07).
Remediation: Deny aws:SecureTransport = false on every bucket. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the log archive and the Restricted buckets instead of MFA Delete, and record that as Cypher's deviation from 2.1.2.

Title: CloudCo has no security contact for Cypher and no support role
Detail: No security alternate contact is registered in any account, so CloudCo's security notices reach an unmonitored billing mailbox. No role holds AWSSupportAccess, so opening a case during an incident needs admin or root.
Remediation: Register security@ as the security contact in all three accounts and create a support role.

Title: Database minor upgrades depend on someone remembering
Detail: Auto minor version upgrade is off on cgi-prod-db. The last minor version was applied manually seven months ago.
Root cause: No platform patching rule: CGI-POL-001 s4.4.3 covers workstations; CGI-POL-008 is unwritten (CG-02).
Remediation: Enable auto minor version upgrade inside the maintenance window. Cover platform patching in CGI-POL-008 (REC-08).
